prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation by chemically designed bifunctional degraders that bring a target protein and an E3 ubiquitin ligase together

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize for induced-proximity protein degraders, credited to Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. The achievement is a new mode of small-molecule action. A designed molecule does not occupy an active site; it forms a ternary complex, and the cell's own ubiquitin-proteasome machinery removes the target. The design variables (ligase ligand, linker, cooperativity) are chemical and measurable, the principle has been reproduced across many ligases and laboratories, and it has opened targets once called undruggable. The round-1 exchange did not weaken this case. The objections raised against it, missing approval and the glue strand, concern the edges of the citation, not the existence or reproducibility of the principle. The chair's question is whether to write a PROTAC-only citation, add a glue part, or defer. I would write PROTAC-only, worded as heterobifunctional degraders, so that it does not claim the cereblon glue mechanism. A two-part prize that adds the glue strand would need Handa, Ito and Gray, which breaks the three-person cap, and I do not think the committee should reach for it just to look complete.
statement.case_against: The credit problem is real and I am not dissolving it. A three-name PROTAC citation leaves out Sakamoto, a coauthor of the founding 2001 paper, and the entire thalidomide-cereblon strand (Handa, Ito, Gray, Kim), which explains an existing drug class. No PROTAC is yet approved, and I am working from memory on clinical status. Base editing is further along in patients, and nanopore sensing is more mature in deployment. If the committee concludes that the PROTAC and glue strands cannot be separated, then a single clean prize on another achievement is more defensible than a contested one on this. I do not currently think that is the case, but I would move if the expert reports show the two strands cannot be separated.

responses.point: Aqvist has moved to Liu alone for base editing and argues that its list is uncontestable, while the degrader credit is split among Crews and Deshaies, Ciulli and the cereblon mechanism, and no degrader is approved.
responses.response: I agree that Liu alone is the cleanest base-editing credit, and it makes B011 a stronger competitor than I judged in round 1; it remains my second choice. I do not accept that the base-editing list is uncontestable, though. Komor and Gaudelli did the experimental work on both founding editors, and Nishida and Kondo have an independent priority claim on cytidine deamination. A Liu-only prize defers those disputes without resolving them. The degrader dispute is also narrower than you suggest: the PROTAC concept and the cereblon glue mechanism are different discoveries, and a citation limited to bifunctional degraders honours the first without claiming the second. I still think the absence of an approval is a weaker test for chemistry than the quantitative ternary-complex evidence.

responses.point: Somfai pairs C-N coupling with a Crews-only degrader credit, arguing that a methods part plus a new modality is a balanced prize and that B038 is the most chemically original biology-facing nomination.
responses.response: I am glad you see the chemical originality of induced proximity, but I cannot support a Crews-only credit. Deshaies's contribution to the PROTAC concept and the 2001 work, and Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structure work, are what turned the idea into a design discipline, so dropping them is hard to defend. I also doubt that C-N coupling adds enough to the 2010 cross-coupling prize. Brzezinski makes the same point, and I find it persuasive. If you accept B038 as a prize in its own right, I would ask you to back the three-name version rather than pairing it with B058, since the pairing has no other supporter and the three-person cap costs Deshaies and Ciulli.

responses.point: Linke asks whether nanopore attribution can be settled and whether nanopore sequencing is chemistry or genomics technology, and he ranks degraders only fifth.
responses.response: You asked whether Deamer's conception can be separated from Branton and Kasianowicz's first translocation experiments. I do not think it can be separated well enough to defend three names. Branton and Kasianowicz showed that a polynucleotide passes through alpha-hemolysin and is read in the ionic current, so leaving them out cuts the history at the point where the measurement principle was shown to work. That is my reason for keeping B003 as an alternative rather than my first choice, even though I rank it second on science. The chemistry-or-genomics question matters less to me than the attribution, since the transduction principle is analytical chemistry. I would accept B003 only if the expert reports give a defensible three-person cut.

responses.point: Chabes ranks degraders first with the same trio, accepts that the glue strand is a competing claim, and notes that base editing is mature and cleaner in attribution.
responses.response: We agree on the trio and on the glue problem. Where I would go further than your statement is the citation wording: I would anchor it on heterobifunctional degraders and the recruitment of an E3 ligase, not on 'the ubiquitin-proteasome system', because the broader phrase invites the claim that glue degraders are covered, and then Handa, Ito and Gray are excluded from a citation that appears to cover their work. I also think we should say openly in the committee that the thalidomide-cereblon mechanism is a separate achievement that a later prize could honour, rather than quietly treating it as outside the question.

responses.point: Sparr proposes a two-part prize pairing phase separation (Hyman, Brangwynne) with Liu-only base editing, and argues that the concept-level citation does not depend on which condensates are true phases.
responses.response: Your distinction between the demonstrated phenomenon and the contested labelling of individual condensates is fair, and I take it more seriously than I did in round 1. I still think the concept is being revised, since evidence for what is functional in cells is not yet settled, and that makes a citation harder to write than one for degraders or base editing. The pairing also costs Rosen and Pappu and Mittag, which you acknowledge. I would rather the committee consider B065 in a later year, as a single three-person part, than attach it now to a base-editing credit that already has its own open priority questions.

responses.point: Zou pairs nitrogenase structure (Rees, Einsle) with Liu-only base editing and argues that the committee should value both a structural landmark and an enabling method.
responses.response: I agree that the FeMo-cofactor structures are a landmark and I take your point that my translational lens can undervalue fundamental mechanism. I do not think a two-part prize is the answer to the lack of a majority, though. The chair noted that nobody besides you has proposed this pairing, and it requires Dean, Seefeldt and Ribbe to be passed over silently. A single clean prize that the committee can defend line by line is better than a combination assembled to collect votes. If the committee ends up with a two-part prize, I would want it justified by the science of both parts and not by the vote count.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports can cleanly separate the PROTAC strand from the thalidomide-cereblon glue strand, and whether Sakamoto's coauthorship of the 2001 paper warrants a name.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC will weigh with a majority as a timing argument, and I am working from memory on clinical status.
Whether base editing, with Liu alone, can overcome the 2020 CRISPR precedent and the Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo credit questions better than B038 overcomes its own.
Whether any configuration will reach five votes, since no position has a majority after round 1.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no personal or institutional tie to Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli or any other shortlisted candidate. My research on peptide and nanoparticle sensing and on biomaterials overlaps thematically with chemical biology, but not with any shortlisted ballot directly, and I do not request recusal.
